results.title: [2508.18442] DenseRec: Revisiting Dense Content Embeddings for Sequential Transformer-based Recommendation

item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports text-enhanced sequential recommendation, but the retrieved papers do not establish gains for a NextItNet text encoder trained entirely from scratch. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) learns recommendations from item text and reports benefits in low-resource and cold-start settings; its pretrained language representations and bidirectional Transformer make it unsuitable as a direct implementation here. [DenseRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18442) projects content embeddings into the item-ID embedding space, supporting content/identity integration, but uses pretrained MiniLM embeddings. Neither result proves that randomly initialized text features improve this benchmark.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis: retain [NextItNet’s residual dilated causal convolutions](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), adding a small, randomly initialized token embedding encoder over available titles/descriptions. Pool tokens, project to the item embedding dimension, and combine with item-ID embeddings through a jointly learned residual gate. Train all components together under the next-item objective; use the same combined representation for history inputs and candidate scoring within one model per category. Shared tokens could transfer interaction supervision across sparse items, although lexical similarity does not establish product compatibility or purchase intent. Compare identity-only, title-only augmentation, and title-plus-description augmentation using the fixed macro validation HR@10. Keep padding representations zero, read the final nonpadding position, and preserve diagnostic interfaces and checkpoint/predictor consistency. This is a proposed adaptation, not a literature-validated improvement."}
